items.stem: Which best describes distributed tracing among the three pillars of observability?

options.text: It tracks a request and its activities across components so you can see where time is spent
options.rationale: Correct: tracing follows a request across components to localize latency and failures.

options.text: It records only counters and gauges such as active request count
It stores individual event records like a single failed operation
options.rationale: That describes logs rather than distributed tracing.

options.text: It is the same as attaching a debugger to production
options.rationale: Tracing is designed to be low-overhead and transparent, unlike invasive debugging.

items.explanation: Correct: tracing follows a request across components to localize latency and failures.

items.stem: Select TWO .NET framework APIs that the .NET OpenTelemetry implementation builds on for instrumentation.

options.rationale: Correct: OTel collects metrics emitted via Meter.
Correct: OTel collects spans produced via ActivitySource/Activity.

options.text: System.Console.WriteLine as the primary telemetry API
options.rationale: Console output is not the structured instrumentation API OTel consumes.

options.text: A custom APM-specific proprietary API required by OTel
options.rationale: OTel avoids APM-specific APIs; it uses the standard .NET APIs.
Thread is not a telemetry API.

items.explanation: Correct: OTel collects metrics emitted via Meter.

items.stem: You want to send .NET traces and metrics to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend without coupling to one vendor. What should you configure?

options.rationale: Correct: OTLP is the vendor-neutral wire protocol for exporting telemetry to compatible backends.

options.text: A vendor-specific SDK in place of OpenTelemetry
options.rationale: A vendor SDK couples you to that vendor, the opposite of the goal.
Console logging does not export telemetry to a backend.
A debugger does not export telemetry and is invasive.

items.explanation: Correct: OTLP is the vendor-neutral wire protocol for exporting telemetry to compatible backends.
